ai.description: *Ichthyophis daribokensis* is a slender caecilian reaching 22 cm. It is dark violet-brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a pale venter. It features 280–290 primary annuli and a terminal shield.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis daribokensis* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, continuous yellow lateral stripe that extends from the snout to the tip of the tail.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis daribokensis* inhabits moist, subtropical broadleaf forests in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya, typically found in damp soil near streams at moderate altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Ichthyophis daribokensis* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis daribokensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of approximately 20–30 eggs in terrestrial nests near water during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis daribokensis* is endemic to the East Garo Hills in Meghalaya, India, where it inhabits tropical forest streams at elevations between 400 and 800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ichthyophis daribokensis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed chirps emitted by males while submerged in shallow forest streams.
